topic: Receipts and payments vs income and expenditure account
question: Distinguish between a Receipts and Payments Account and an Income and Expenditure Account prepared by a not-for-profit organisation.
sources: Standard accounting principles for financial statements of not-for-profit organisations (ICAI Foundation syllabus)
Accrual basis of accounting (AS 1 fundamental accounting assumption)

points.label: Nature of account
points.description: A Receipts and Payments Account is a summary of the cash book (a real account); an Income and Expenditure Account is like a profit and loss account (a nominal account).
points.basis: Accounting principle: nature of the two accounts of a not-for-profit organisation

points.label: Basis of accounting
points.description: Receipts and Payments records actual cash received and paid during the year (cash basis); Income and Expenditure records income and expenses of the year on accrual basis, including outstanding and prepaid items.
points.basis: Accrual assumption under AS 1 applied to the Income and Expenditure Account

points.label: Capital and revenue items
points.description: Receipts and Payments includes both capital and revenue items; Income and Expenditure includes only revenue items of the current period.
points.basis: Accounting principle: capital and revenue distinction

points.label: Balances and result
points.description: Receipts and Payments starts with the opening cash and bank balance and ends with the closing balance; Income and Expenditure has no opening balance and ends with a surplus (income over expenditure) or deficit.
points.basis: Accounting principle: preparation of the two accounts

points.label: Non-cash items
points.description: Non-cash items like depreciation do not appear in Receipts and Payments but are shown in Income and Expenditure.
points.basis: Accounting principle: treatment of non-cash expenses
